children: Enterprise software and business AI provider SAP

traded at $238.40, down 0.91%, at 10:24 a.m. ET on Friday. According to AD HOC News, BMO raised its price target to $265 from $235 and maintained Outperform. That puts the target roughly 11.2% above the share price. The analyst sees room to climb. Investors still need execution.

The business has momentum. SAP's third-quarter release reported 24.1 billion in current cloud backlog, up 26% at constant currencies, alongside 25% cloud revenue growth. Cloud ERP Suite revenue increased 28% on the same basis, while operating profit rose 18% under both IFRS and adjusted measures. Quarterly revenue topped 10 billion for the first time, and adjusted operating profit crossed 3 billion. Those milestones put real earnings behind the cloud story.

The valuation leaves something to prove. A GF Score of 90/100 signals broad fundamental strength, while a 29.15 price-to-earnings ratio makes sustained earnings growth central to the investment case. BMO's target increase amounts to 12.8%, but a higher target does not convert contracts into sales. The next test is whether SAP can turn its growing backlog into revenue while keeping profit growth strong.

title: SAP Stocks Face 24.1 Billion Backlog Test After BMO Revaluation
